figures.caption: IX-F1. Three accelerator paths and one qualification gate. A serving engine depends on compatible backend integration, kernels, runtime, driver and hardware. Intel GPU, Gaudi and client NPU are distinct paths. The GPU column includes both PyTorch XPU and engine-native SYCL alternatives. Solid arrows mean dependencies; dashed arrows bring the complete path to qualification. Neither means benchmark timing. Device enumeration alone does not validate model correctness, memory residency, collectives or an SLO.
figures.alt_text: Three separate columns descend from serving engine to backend entry, kernels and runtime, and hardware. The Intel GPU column offers torch.xpu or engine-native SYCL. Gaudi uses hpu and its own stack. Client NPU uses the OpenVINO NPU plugin. All columns lead to a gate requiring a complete model-serving configuration, including memory, operators, correctness, isolation, collectives when used and a measured SLO.
figures.data_classification: Original conceptual diagram; no measured performance data
